findings.source_location: Section 2, equations (2)-(4), source lines 65-77; Section 4 and Appendix A, especially lines 53-56 and 454-474.
findings.finding: The model summary omits the defining update rule and leaves the threshold-search method at the level of 'identifies epsilon values'. The article defines opinions on [0,1], the inclusive insider condition |x_i(t)-x_j(t)| <= epsilon (including the agent itself), and simultaneous next-period replacement by the arithmetic mean of all insiders. An epsilon-switch is the smallest larger confidence value equal to the minimum distance to an outsider over the process; a finite switch list segments confidence values into intervals that induce identical processes. Exact arithmetic is needed to determine these boundaries without rounding errors.
findings.required_fix: State the opinion domain, inclusive insider set, synchronous mean update, switch definition, and exact-fraction requirement. Keep the finite-switch claim qualified: the article says finiteness for all start distributions is conjectured (Appendix A, Analytical Note 6), though its algorithm terminated for every case tested; the article establishes finite primary switches. The existing statement that the full threshold algorithm is omitted does not identify these defining mechanics.
findings.correction_status: addressed in note; independent re-audit pending

findings.source_location: Krackhardt (1987), §3.2, p. 116, primary PDF: row-dominated LAS R'_ij = R_ij_i; column-dominated LAS R'_ij = R_ij_j. Consensus aggregation uses all perceivers; the case example is described on p. 119.
findings.finding: The note says LAS 'combines reports for a focal actor from other perceivers.' That is incorrect. LAS is based on reports by the members of the dyad itself: i's report (row-dominated) or j's report (column-dominated). It is not an aggregation of other informants' reports. The consensus structure is the all-perceiver aggregation. In the case illustration, the LAS is the intersection of i's and j's reports and CS uses a 0.5 threshold across 21 respondents.
findings.required_fix: Replace the LAS sentence with the two explicit variants and distinguish them from consensus aggregation. Cite §3.2/p. 116; if describing the case, cite the p. 119 threshold/intersection example.
findings.correction_status: addressed in note; independent re-audit pending

findings.source_location: §3.2, model components; §§3.3-3.4, relationship trust; §§3.14-3.23, agent strategies and model-control algorithm; §§3.25-3.27, parameters and outputs. Primary HTML lines 134-206, 208-294, 298-314.
findings.finding: The summary omits several defining mechanics and the update order while explicitly deferring all equations and parameter settings. Each agent receives a round-robin turn; a forage/social turn is selected by the FM ratio; a social turn picks a stranger versus existing tie based on N_t,i/P; the selected alter responds cooperatively or defects; directed relationship trust is updated, then trust wanes. Four alter-selection strategies are specified (strong, medium, weak, staged), and trust has linear/log variants with explicit experimental values. Strong/medium/weak output layers are operationally defined by trust terciles. The global defection parameter does not retain relationship-specific defection histories (explicit limitation §5.8). These details are central to the simulation behavior and cannot be elided as generic partner selection.
findings.required_fix: Expand the model description or provide pseudocode capturing turn scheduling, forage/social choice, new/existing alter probabilities, strategy-based selection, response, directed trust update, waning order, parameter variants, tercile outcome definitions, and the global-defection limitation. State any further simplification explicitly and name the source sections/equations.
findings.correction_status: addressed in note; independent re-audit pending
